headline: ハンサム is the English word “handsome” in katakana.
根, “root”, is from Old Japanese and first cited to the Kojiki of 712.
シャワー is borrowed from English “shower”.
ショック is the English word “shock” in katakana.
旅, “travel, trip”, may be cognate with 度 (tabi), with the same pitch accent and ancient vowel values.
プリント, “print, handout”, is borrowed from English “print”.
留める shares its reading with 止める, “to stop”, and 停める, “to park (a car)”, as cognates.
パーティー is the English word “party” in katakana.
盆 is short for 盂蘭盆 (Urabon), which some dictionaries trace to Sanskrit ullambana, purportedly “hanging upside-down”.
パイプ is borrowed from English “pipe”.
胃, “stomach”, was /wi/ before /i/, and comes from Middle Chinese.
クラシック is the English word “classic” in katakana.
タイプ is the English word “type” in katakana.
羨ましい is 羨む (urayamu, “to envy, to be jealous of”) plus しい (-shii), an adjectivizing suffix.
スーパーマーケット is the English word “supermarket” in katakana.
埃, “dust”, is compared in the source with 誇り (hokori, “pride”).
コンクリート is the English word “concrete” in katakana.
呼び掛ける is 呼ぶ (yobu, “to call”) plus 掛ける (kakeru).
マーケット is borrowed from English “market”.
軍, “army”, shifted from /kʲun/ to /ɡun/ after it came from Middle Chinese.
マッチ is the English word “match” in katakana.
パンツ, “underpants”, is borrowed from English “pants” and first cited to a text from 1896.
悲しむ is 悲しい (kanashii, “sad”) plus む (-mu).
タオル, “(hand) towel”, is the English word “towel” in katakana.
取り出す is 取る (toru, “to take”) plus 出す (dasu, “to put out”).
スポーツ, “sport(s)”, is borrowed from the English plural “sports”.
量, “quantity, amount”, comes from Middle Chinese 量 (MC ljangH, “measure”).
タイトル is borrowed from English “title”.
スタンド is borrowed from English “stand” and first attested in 1902.
野, “field”, is from Old Japanese, written ⟨no₁⟩ in the source.
